2012_041_100212regmtg.paragraph: The Troy School District Board of Education met in regular session at 7:00 p.m. on October 2, 2012 at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, taking up recognitions, a consent agenda carrying the August 2012 Treasurer's Report, personnel and curriculum items, a storm water management plan, and board committee assignments. The weightiest action was a refunding resolution authorizing 2012 Refunding Bonds in an aggregate principal amount not to exceed $47,000,000 to advance refund the district's 2004 School Building and Site and Refunding Bonds dated August 12, 2004, with estimated savings put at $4,920,334. The August Treasurer's Report showed total disbursements in the period of $5,125,380.16.

**Meeting.** Troy School District (Oakland County, Michigan) Board of Education Regular Meeting, October 2, 2012, 7:00 p.m., Services Building, 4420 Livernois; district offices at 4400 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098, 248.823.4000. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) Mondays and Wednesdays at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. and posted at http://vimeo.com/troyschools.

**Recognitions.** First-semester student representatives Aishawarya Singh (Athens), Asja Kepes (International Academy-East), Miranda Wilson (Niles Community High School), and Patty Durell (Troy High). More than 400 Troy students were honored as Advanced Placement Scholars, with twelve named for earning the honor as juniors. A resolution recognized two National Achievement Scholarship semifinalists (Aaron Faison, Taylor Matthew) and fifty-nine National Merit Scholarship semifinalists, to be presented at a November 7th reception.

**Consent agenda.** Minutes of the September 4, 2012 regular meeting and the September 18, 2012 workshop; the August 2012 Treasurer's Report; and a non-renewal teacher contract. The September 4 minutes record Motions 12-086, 12-087, and 12-088 each passing 7-0, including rescheduling the November 6, 2012 meeting to November 13, 2012 at 6:00 p.m. The district received ASBO International's Certificate of Excellence in Financial Reporting for the CAFR for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2011, its twenty-third consecutive year.

General Fund (101, 120, 122, 140) August year-to-date for fiscal 2013: adopted revenue budget $129,234,265 against actual $10,042,357 (92.23% uncollected); adopted expenditure budget $132,398,263 against actual $7,485,923 with $95,709,266 encumbered and $29,203,074 available (22.06%). Excess revenue over (under) expenditures is (3,163,998); fund balance moves from $20,591,023 on July 1, 2012 to a projected $17,427,025 on June 30, 2013. Debt Service Funds 304/306/307 project a fund balance of $(3,129,052) from $(1,825,694).

**Bond refunding (Item 8.B).** The resolution designates the 2012 Refunding Bonds, not to exceed $47,000,000, issued under Act 451 PA 1976 and Act 34 PA 2001, in $5,000 denominations maturing May 1, with Clark Hill PLC as bond counsel, Stauder, Barch & Associates, Inc. as financial advisor, and Stifel, Nicolaus & Company, Incorporated as senior managing underwriter or placement agent. The Stauder Barch analysis as of September 13, 2012 prices a $43,585,000 issue dated and delivered 12/15/12 at a net interest cost of 2.11513% and average life of 6.710, depositing $43,432,901.00 to escrow to call $40,500,000 of the 2004 bonds on 5/1/14. Net present value savings are $4,531,850, or 10.40% of the current issue and 11.19% of the previous issue; the maximum debt levy falls from 4.95 mills to 3.07 mills.

**Other items.** Storm water: the district ceased being nested under the City of Troy's coverage on February 9, 2012, entered an Administrative Consent Order with the Michigan DEQ on June 6, 2012, and adopted policies under NPDES General Permit MIS049000. Personnel: probationary contracts for Katie Lamansky (.8 FTE math/science, Boulan Park Middle School) and Cara Lebryk (.3 FTE vocal music, Wattles/Morse), plus termination of Noah Elkins effective September 7, 2012. Board negotiating teams were named for TEA, TESA, and TESPA, all expiring June 30, 2013. Fleming, Miletti, Philippart, and Schmidt were certified as MASB delegates for the November 8, 2012 Delegate Assembly. The meeting closed with a resolution to enter closed session under the Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c).

Troy School District, Oakland County, Michigan, convened its Board of Education Regular Meeting at 7:00 p.m. on October 2, 2012 in the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, with district offices at 4400 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098 (248.823.4000, www.troy.k12.mi.us). Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) Mondays and Wednesdays at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. except July and August, and streamed at http://vimeo.com/troyschools.

**Recognitions.** First-semester student representatives were Aishawarya Singh (Athens High School), Asja Kepes (International Academy-East), Miranda Wilson (Niles Community High School since January 2011, anticipating graduation January 2014), and Patty Durell (Troy High). More than 400 students were honored for Advanced Placement exam performance, twelve of them for earning the honor as juniors: Aditya Achanta, Dorothy Chen, Kathleen Chen, Tyler Garling, Peter Hao, Lawrence Kim, Jacob Lourim, Sara Ma, Rohit Maruthi, Kabir Singh, Phillip Yang and Michael Yu. A resolution signed the second day of October, 2012 honored semifinalists: the National Achievement Scholarship Program drew more than 160,000 entrants with only 1,600 semifinalists, of whom Troy had two, Aaron Faison and Taylor Matthew; the National Merit Scholarship Program drew more than one million students from some 22,000 high schools with 16,000 semifinalists scoring in the top one and one-half percent on the PSAT, of whom Troy had fifty-nine. Certificates were to be presented at a reception on November 7th.

**Consent agenda and minutes.** Items were the September 4, 2012 minutes, September 18, 2012 workshop minutes, the August 2012 Treasurer's Report, and a non-renewal teacher contract. The September 4 meeting was called to order by President Philippart at 7:01 p.m. with Philippart, Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Miletti, Schmidt and Underwood present, plus Superintendent Fowler and administrators Birmingham, Colligan, Jolly, Lesser, Machesky, Rajter and Witt. ASBO International's Certificate of Excellence in Financial Reporting honored the Comprehensive Annual Financial Report for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2011, the twenty-third year in a row, with Mark Rajter, Assistant Superintendent for Business Services, recognized. Motion 12-086 approved July 17, 2011 special minutes, August 14, 2012 minutes and an Adobe software bid award, 7 yes / 0 no; Motion 12-087 approved 20 new hires, 7-0; Motion 12-088 rescheduled the November 6, 2012 meeting to November 13, 2012 at 6:00 p.m., 7-0. Dr. Rich Machesky reported overall district enrollment increased by 60 students compared with the September 2011 count, with Official Membership Day on Wednesday, October 3rd. The meeting adjourned at 8:37 p.m.; minutes were submitted by Todd Miletti, Secretary. The September 18 workshop ran 6:00 p.m. to 10:00 p.m. and covered a 7th hour proposal, stormwater regulations, special education processes, refunding of bonds, superintendent evaluation and committee assignments.

**Personnel and curriculum.** Item 5.D acknowledged the termination of Noah Elkins, Athens High School French teacher, effective September 7, 2012 for abandonment of his position at the start of the 2012/2013 school year. Item 6.A approved probationary contracts for Katie Lamansky (.8 FTE math/science, Boulan Park Middle School; B.S. Eastern Michigan University, August 2006; Michigan Provisional Certificate August 2012; Fulton County Schools, Alpharetta, GA, August 2007-June 2012; resident of Brighton) and Cara Lebryk (.3 FTE vocal music, Wattles/Morse; B.M. Oakland University, December 2009; certificate May 2010; Holly Area Schools and Utica Community Schools; resident of Orion). Item 6.B named Jasen Witt chief spokesperson for all three units, with Mark Rajter, Jan Keeling and Richard Machesky on the TEA team; Richard Machesky, Monica Papasian and Sara Konieczka on TESA; and Mark Rajter, Jan Keeling and Sara Konieczka on TESPA, all three MEA/NEA agreements expiring June 30, 2013. Item 7.A approved the 2012/2013 Sex Education Advisory Board, co-chaired by Baker Middle School principal Larry Hahn and parent Nicole Jenkins, with teachers Mary McDermott and Kevin Wilson, Rev. Jack Mannschreck of Big Beaver United Methodist Church, nurse Lois Winer of the Oakland Health Department, seven parents, a resident, and students Heather Turner and Dejan Jenkins. Item 7.B was a professional development report by Anne Mull, Director of Instruction and Assessment, covering literacy (Lester Laminack K-2, Frank Serafini 3-5, Carol Jago), mathematics (Big Ideas Mathematics, SMARTER-BALANCED, Common Core alignment), science claim-evidence-reasoning writing, and social studies, where 12 trained middle school teachers are to grow to 24 in grades 6-12 with sessions on October 31, November 14 and November 28, 2012.

**Storm water (Item 8.A).** Before February 9, 2012 the district was nested under the City of Troy's Certificate of Coverage; the Michigan DEQ then required its own coverage, and an Administrative Consent Order was entered June 6, 2012. The plan follows the 2003 MS4 Jurisdictional General Permit and its six minimum management measures under NPDES General Permit number MIS049000, requiring a construction site permit and structural controls for new development or redevelopment disturbing more than 1 acre.

**Refunding of bonds (Item 8.B).** The cover memo states that at current rates the estimated savings are $4,920,334. The resolution authorizes 2012 Refunding Bonds not to exceed $47,000,000 to advance refund the 2004 School Building and Site and Refunding Bonds dated August 12, 2004, under Act 451 PA 1976 and Act 34 PA 2001, in $5,000 denominations maturing May 1, book-entry through Cede & Co. and The Depository Trust Company, payable from taxes levied without limitation as to rate or amount under Article IX, Sections 6 and 16 of the Michigan Constitution of 1963. Clark Hill PLC is bond counsel, Stauder, Barch & Associates, Inc. of 3989 Research Park Drive, Ann Arbor is financial advisor, and Stifel, Nicolaus & Company, Incorporated is senior managing underwriter or placement agent; qualification is sought under Act 92 PA 2005 through the Michigan School Bond Qualification and Loan Program, with continuing disclosure through EMMA under Rule 15c2-12 beginning with the fiscal year ending June 30, 2013. The escrow agreement recites $55,315,000 of Prior Bonds outstanding, names The Bank of New York Mellon Trust Company, N.A. as Refunded Bonds Paying Agent, directs notice no later than April 1, 2014 to call the Refunded Bonds on May 1, 2014, and requires any successor escrow agent to have combined capital and surplus of at least $50,000,000.

The Stauder Barch analysis as of September 13, 2012 covers a $43,585,000 issue dated and delivered 12/15/12. Existing debt before refunding was $103,580,000 of principal and $138,241,500 of principal and interest, combining the 2004 bonds (original $98,870,000, outstanding $55,315,000, net interest cost 5.000%, maturities from 2015 callable 5/1/14 at 100) and the 2006 bonds (original $53,545,000, outstanding $48,265,000). Principal called is $40,500,000 with debt service to escrow of $43,537,500 and no call premium. Sources and uses: par $43,585,000.00; deposit to escrow account $43,432,901.00; underwriter's discount $15,000.00 at 0.034%; costs of issuance estimate $135,744.15; miscellaneous $1,354.85; arbitrage yield 2.11%, escrow yield 0.18%, estimated negative arbitrage $1,105,271. The new bonds carry an average coupon of 2.11000%, net interest cost 2.11513%, true interest cost 2.11576%, arbitrage yield 2.11016%, effective interest cost 2.16706%, bond years 292,465.44 and average life 6.710, with gross interest cost $6,171,020.88 and total payments of $49,756,020.88. Present value of refunded bonds is $48,115,509 less present value of refunding bonds of $43,585,014, for gross present value savings of $4,530,495 and net present value savings of $4,531,850, equal to 10.40% of the current issue and 11.19% of the previous issue; annual savings total $4,918,979 and cumulative savings $4,920,334. The maximum levy falls from 4.95 mills before refunding to 3.07 after, an increase of (1.88), against a current levy of 4.95 mills. Ad valorem taxable value history: $4,448,741,027 (2007), $4,443,349,700 (2008), $4,383,001,954 (2009), $3,886,495,631 (2010), $3,566,967,490 (2011) and $3,458,912,080 (2012), average growth -4.81%. The escrow portfolio holds SLGS of $983,841 at 0.110%, $973,888 at 0.150% and $41,475,172 at 0.180%, totaling $43,432,901.00 at a 12/15/12 settlement.

**Other business.** Item 10.A adopted 2012-2013 board committee memberships revised September 18, 2012: Senior Advisory Committee (Fleming), Troy Community Coalition (Schmidt), Troy Foundation for Educational Excellence (Fleming), Troy Youth Assistance (Schmidt), NCA District Team (Schmidt), Safety Committee (Edmunds, Hauff), Diversity Council (Underwood), District Technology Committee (Miletti), Policy Committee (Edmunds, Hauff, Philippart) and Superintendent Evaluation Committee (Fleming, Miletti, Philippart). Item 10.B certified Mrs. Paula Fleming, Mr. Todd Miletti, Ms. Nancy Philippart and Mr. Karl Schmidt as delegates to the MASB 2012 Delegate Assembly on November 8, 2012. Item 10.C presented Dr. Fowler's 2012/2013 superintendent goals: college and career readiness in literacy, mathematics, science and social studies; continued interventions for the lowest performing subgroups; preparation for a Bond Election in November 2013 covering facility needs, technology upgrades and bus replacement; and completion of a data processing review with total cost analysis. Item 11.A resolved to enter closed session on an attorney-client privilege item as permitted by the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c), with roll call of Fleming, Hauff, Miletti, Philippart, Schmidt, Underwood and Edmunds.
